status.description:
The status of the video.

- `draft` - the project was created but has not been submitted for rendering
- `queued` - the job is waiting for an available server
- `rendering` - the job is being processed; the `video.started` webhook event fires when rendering begins
- `complete` - the job finished successfully; fires `video.completed`
- `error` - the job failed during processing; fires `video.errored`
- `canceled` - the job was manually canceled (for example from the Magic Hour web app)

**Note:** `rendering`, `complete`, and `error` have matching webhook events; `canceled` does not - a canceled job emits no webhook event, so poll this endpoint to detect cancellation.

info.title: Magic Hour Webhook
info.description:
## Introduction 

Configuring a webhook allow Magic Hour to notify you whenever an event occurs in your account. To get started, create a webhook [here](https://magichour.ai/developer?tab=webhooks&utm_source=docs&utm_medium=referral&utm_campaign=webhook-reference).

API documentation can be found [here](https://docs.magichour.ai/webhook-reference).

If you have any questions, please reach out to us via [discord](https://discord.gg/JX5rgsZaJp).

## Securing your endpoint

Events includes two headers to help verify the authenticity of the payload. 
- `magic-hour-event-signature` - A 64-character hexadecimal HMAC-SHA256 signature. Use the complete webhook secret, not an API key, to sign the timestamp header, a period, and the exact raw request body.
- `magic-hour-event-timestamp` - Unix time in seconds for this delivery attempt. Reject missing or invalid timestamps; a five-minute window before or after the current time is recommended to limit replay.

Verify the signature and timestamp before accepting production events. Read the entire raw request body before parsing JSON.

To compute the signature to verify:
1. Create a `signed_payload` by concatenating:
      - the timestamp header exactly as received
      - the character `.`
      - the exact raw UTF-8 request body, including both `type` and `payload`

Do not parse and re-stringify the body or sign `payload` alone.

2. Compute HMAC-SHA256 with the complete webhook secret as the key and `signed_payload` as the message. Do not strip the secret prefix or use your API key.
3. Compare its hexadecimal digest with `magic-hour-event-signature` using a constant-time comparison. Reject missing or invalid headers, mismatches, and timestamps outside your configured past/future tolerance. See the [secure-handler guide](https://docs.magichour.ai/integration/webhook/secure-handler) for complete Python and Node examples.

## Retry behavior

Failed deliveries, including timeouts and non-`2XX` responses, are scheduled after 1, 2, 4, 8... minutes, capped at 60 minutes, until the event is more than 24 hours old. These are scheduled delays, not guaranteed delivery times. Verify and durably accept the event before returning `2XX`; acknowledge promptly. Timestamp and signature are regenerated for every delivery attempt.

Disabled webhooks do not receive pending deliveries. Those events remain subject to the same expiry; re-enabling a webhook allows pending events to resume before expiry.
